# yamo_frames.asm: Yamo animation frames: 1-bit sprite graphics, 8 or 16 pixels wide

Range `$5D91-$6282`. Source: [yamo_frames.asm](../../../src/yamo_frames.asm). Index: [the reference](../index.md).

## Names

<a id="yamo_frame_25"></a>
### [`yamo_frame_25`](../../../src/yamo_frames.asm#L13) `$5D91-$5DBA`

*data*

Format of every animation frame: 1 bit per pixel, row after row from the top, 1 byte per row (8 pixels) or 2 bytes per row (16 pixels, left byte first) as frame_is_wide says. The game shows the sprites X-expanded, so a frame is 16 or 32 screen pixels wide. The sprite builder copy_sprite_frame copies a frame into the left 1 or 2 bytes of each row of a sprite block and clears the rest; it never mirrors, so each facing has its own frame. At cold start build_contact_masks builds a 96-byte contact mask from each pose (both sprites OR-ed, every pixel doubled) at $9000-$9FBF and contact_masks_high. The bytes between frames that no table entry covers are unused padding. Yamo frame 25 (global frame 95). 16 pixels wide, 20 rows of 2 bytes (the mask builder reads 21), colour green ($F5). Second sprite of pose frame 94. Picture: flying kick, leg stretched out (state $0C or $0D, timer below 10).

- **Entry of:** [`frame_gfx_lo`](../tables.md#frame_gfx_lo)
